subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox container exits immediately when no-new-privileges is applied (exec /usr/bin/sleep: operation not permitted)

question: Should Docker sandboxes keep `no-new-privileges` unconditional, or should OpenClaw add an explicit dangerous recovery path for hosts where that flag prevents sandbox startup?
rationale: The user-visible failure is valid, but the obvious mitigations change sandbox hardening or add a new config surface, which requires maintainer security posture approval rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Add audited dangerous opt-out
options.body: Keep `no-new-privileges` as the default, add a clearly named operator opt-out with security audit/status reporting, and require real Docker proof for both default and opt-out paths.

options.title: Diagnostic-only for now
options.body: Keep the hardening unconditional and improve status/session errors so affected operators can identify the host incompatibility without weakening isolation.

options.title: Fix image/runtime compatibility
options.body: Investigate and repair the bundled image or runtime assumptions so `no-new-privileges` works on affected hosts without adding an opt-out.

recommendation.title: Add audited dangerous opt-out
recommendation.body: Keep `no-new-privileges` as the default, add a clearly named operator opt-out with security audit/status reporting, and require real Docker proof for both default and opt-out paths.
